subject.title: [Feature] Queue prompts when API limits prevent an immediate response

question: Should OpenClaw implement this as a core-owned durable provider-capacity prompt queue, and which overlapping partial PR should become the base for that design?
rationale: The permanent behavior crosses provider failover, auth-profile cooldowns, session state, gateway/channel delivery, persistence, and visible status, so automation should not choose the product boundary or persistence semantics from overlapping PRs.

options.title: Approve one durable core queue
options.body: Use a SQLite-backed core queue/replay design and accept only related PR work that fits that single path.

options.title: Land partial mitigations only
options.body: Allow narrower provider cooldown or followup-restart recovery PRs to land while keeping full prompt replay uncommitted.

options.title: Reject durable replay
options.body: Close the direction as too risky or out of scope and rely on surfaced failure/cooldown status plus user re-prompting.

recommendation.title: Approve one durable core queue
recommendation.body: Use a SQLite-backed core queue/replay design and accept only related PR work that fits that single path.

likelyOwner.reason: The followup/runtime consolidation history makes steipete the best available routing candidate for the cross-cutting product boundary decision.
